method_note: Text-level only. No lake build or comparator run (shared checkout; the release Lean is trusted as published per PLAN). Dependency chain from data/items/312_lean.json (fixed extractor) plus hand reading of the Lean files. Item not yet in data/eureka_shortlist.json, so there is no lean_decls hint; the novelty.json C1 'lean' field was used instead. arxiv.org blocked; external evidence is WebSearch snippets only, marked unverified where not read in full.
lean_status_why: The device itself is in the Lean verbatim (cylinderNode = stationary below n / critical at n / completedCylinder above n; cylinder_oneSided_contractible takes the higher-index invariant H : ExpansionContraction hC q (n+1)), and it is load-bearing for the comparator (cylinderPathData dominates 64.8% of the 856-declaration proof DAG). The induction runs on a reformulated invariant (contractibility preservation for J_{>=r}-cofibrations, not 'J_n pushouts are weak equivalences'), with trees and joint lifting replaced by other lemmas.
lean_gaps: Induction invariant differs. The paper inducts on E(q,n), 'every J_n pushout from a cellular object in A_q is a weak equivalence'. The Lean inducts (strong induction on q-r) on ExpansionContraction hC q r: every J_{>=r}-cofibration from a cofibrant contractible cutoff model has a contractible target. A weak equivalence appears only at the end (exactBoundaryTest_of_cutoff_path). The bootstrap shape is the same: index-n cylinders are made contractible by the index-(n+1) statement.
No W calculus (division, change of boundary, two-out-of-three) is formalized. The Lean uses only ExactBoundaryTest, HasFillers and the (3)=>(1) direction of the weak-equivalence test.

Tree contractibility (paper Prop 3.7, J_{n+1} duplication) is replaced by whisker/reverse-whisker shapes plus free_hasFillers_of_top_homotopy, a small-object factorization and retract. Cylinder contractibility (Prop 4.2) is proved for the one-sided objects A_j^eps through whisker presentations and comparison maps (cylinder_oneSided_contractible), not by the paper's exact skeletal gluing formula as written.

Joint lifting is required for every J_k with k >= r (CutoffPathData.joint), which is stronger than the paper's J_n alone. It is proved with criticalJoint_retract and fullCylinder_joint instead of the four-vertex tree B.

The path object is per object and need not be functorial. CutoffPathData is chosen for each Y. fullCylinder is the presheaf Hom(cylinderRealization S, Y), interpreted through a section of cylinderProjection obtained by Classical.choose from the coherator's lifting property. It is then reflected into A_q (reflectedCylinder). The paper builds a functor P.
The P_j are defined for every j in N, not only j <= q. Above q, cutoff models have unique fillers, so this is harmless.
Scope: the comparator is exactly Theorem 1.1 (Henry's pushout conjecture). The homotopy hypothesis (Cor 5.2) and the semi-model structure (Cor 5.1) are not formalized.

Non-vacuity: no IsCoherator instance is constructed anywhere, so a Lean speedup experiment over this library should first build one (for example a free tower from Theta_0) to avoid testing a vacuous hypothesis set.

lean_source.name: OAI.Grothendieck.GlobularTheory.Model.ExpansionContraction
lean_source.text:
def ExpansionContraction {C : GlobularTheory.{v}} (hC : C.IsCoherator)
    (q r : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ {X Y : CutoffModels C q} (i : X ⟶ Y),
    (sourceClass hC q r).rlp.llp i → Cofibrant hC q X →
      X.obj.underlying.HasFillers → Y.obj.underlying.HasFillers
lean_source.role: Lean induction invariant (paper E(q,r) reformulated): J_{>=r}-cofibrations from cofibrant contractible cutoff models have contractible targets.

lean_source.name: OAI.Grothendieck.CylinderNode
lean_source.text:
structure CylinderNode {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] (D : GlobularFrame K) (j : ℕ) where
  bd : K
  obj : K
  inc : bd ⟶ obj
  bdEnd : Bool → (D.bd j ⟶ bd)
  endpoint : Bool → (D.obj j ⟶ obj)
  comm : ∀ ε, bdEnd ε ≫ inc = D.inc j ≫ endpoint ε
lean_source.role: One level j of a coglobular cylinder: boundary object, object P_j, two endpoint maps from the disk frame.

lean_source.name: OAI.Grothendieck.CylinderNode.critical
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def critical (D : GlobularFrame K) (n : ℕ) : CylinderNode D n where
  bd := D.bd n
  obj := D.obj (n+1)
  inc := D.inc n ≫ D.diagram.source n
  bdEnd _ := 𝟙 _
  endpoint ε := if ε then D.diagram.target n else D.diagram.source n
  comm ε := ...
lean_source.role: P_n = D_{n+1} with endpoints the source and target n-faces.

lean_source.name: OAI.Grothendieck.CylinderNode.stationary
lean_source.text:
def stationary (D : GlobularFrame K) (j : ℕ) : CylinderNode D j where
  bd := D.bd j
  obj := D.obj j
  inc := D.inc j
  bdEnd _ := 𝟙 _
  endpoint _ := 𝟙 _
  comm _ := by simp
lean_source.role: P_j = D_j with identity endpoints for j < n (stationary below n).

lean_source.name: OAI.Grothendieck.GlobularTheory.Model.cylinderFactor
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def cylinderFactor (j : ℕ) (B : CutoffModels C q)
    (e : Bool → (cutoffBoundary hC q j ⟶ B)) := by
  let := cutoff_hasColimits hC q
  let := cutoff_hasLimits hC q
  let := boundaryClass_smallObject hC q (n+1)
  exact MorphismProperty.factorizationData (boundaryClass hC q (n+1)).rlp.llp
    (boundaryClass hC q (n+1)).rlp
    (terminal.from (TwoEndpoints.obj (cutoffI hC q j) e))
lean_source.role: Small-object factorization of A_j^{01} -> 1 against the upper boundary inclusions I_k, k >= n+1.

lean_source.name: OAI.Grothendieck.GlobularTheory.Model.completedCylinder
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def completedCylinder (j : ℕ) (B : CutoffModels C q)
    (e : Bool → (cutoffBoundary hC q j ⟶ B)) : CylinderNode (cutoffDiskFrame hC q) j := by
  let := cutoff_hasColimits hC q
  let F := cylinderFactor hC q n j B e
  exact
    { bd := B
      obj := F.Z
      inc := TwoEndpoints.base (cutoffI hC q j) e ≫ F.i
      bdEnd := e
      endpoint ε := TwoEndpoints.endpoint (cutoffI hC q j) e ε ≫ F.i
      comm ε := by erw [← Category.assoc, TwoEndpoints.condition, Category.assoc] }
lean_source.role: Upper level P_j (j > n): the completed two-endpoint object.

theorem cylinder_oneSided_contractible (hnq : n ≤ q) (H : ExpansionContraction hC q (n+1)) :
    ∀ j, n < j → ∀ ε : Bool,
      Cofibrant hC q (GlobularFrame.oneSided (cylinderEndpoint hC q n ε) j) ∧
      (GlobularFrame.oneSided (cylinderEndpoint hC q n ε) j).obj.underlying.HasFillers ∧
      (sourceClass hC q (n+1)).rlp.llp (GlobularFrame.oneSidedMap (cylinderEndpoint hC q n ε) j) := ...
lean_source.role: Bootstrap lemma: with H = ExpansionContraction q (n+1), the one-sided objects A_j^eps are cofibrant and contractible and A_j^eps -> P_j is an upper J-cofibration (paper Lemma 4.1/Prop 4.2).

lean_source.name: OAI.Grothendieck.GlobularTheory.Model.CutoffPathData
lean_source.text:
structure CutoffPathData {C : GlobularTheory.{v}} (hC : C.IsCoherator)
    (q r : ℕ) (Y : CutoffModels C q) where
  P : CutoffModels C q
  p₀ : P ⟶ Y
  p₁ : P ⟶ Y
  lifts₀ : (boundaryClass hC q 0).rlp p₀
  lifts₁ : (boundaryClass hC q 0).rlp p₁
  joint : ∀ k, r ≤ k → ∀ (t : cutoffDisk hC q k ⟶ P)
    (u₀ u₁ : cutoffDisk hC q (k+1) ⟶ Y),
    t ≫ p₀ = cutoffJ hC q k ≫ u₀ → t ≫ p₁ = cutoffJ hC q k ≫ u₁ →
    ∃ l : cutoffDisk hC q (k+1) ⟶ P,
      cutoffJ hC q k ≫ l = t ∧ l ≫ p₀ = u₀ ∧ l ≫ p₁ = u₁
lean_source.role: The partial path object interface: endpoints lift all I_j, jointly lift J_k for k >= r.

speedup_targets.title: S1. Lanari's operations on globular cylinders (compositions, identities, inverses, approximate interpretation)
speedup_targets.statement: For a Grothendieck infinity-groupoid Y, the coglobular cylinder objects represent path cells carrying compositions, identities and inverses compatible with the endpoints; Lanari interprets these and leaves the interpretation of all higher operations open.
speedup_targets.reference: Lanari, 'Towards a globular path object for weak infinity-groupoids', JPAA 224 (2020), arXiv:1805.00156, Defs 5.2-5.3, 6.1, Prop 6.2, Thm 6.5. Lanari 2018 (arXiv:1809.07923) Thm 4.10 is the dimension-3 sibling. Taylor arXiv:2609.20860 gives an isomorphic presentation of Lanari's cylinder (abstract only).
speedup_targets.status: known (partial results); the full interpretation is open in Lanari's setting
speedup_targets.current_size: Lanari 2020: a JPAA paper, page count unverified (about 30-40 pp. by snippet). No Lean anywhere. The OAI analogue for its own P_j is cylinderInterpretation plus FullCylinder, a few hundred lines.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: The device replaces explicit operation-by-operation constructions with one lifting argument. Once P(S) is contractible, every generator of the coherator is interpreted on Hom(P_j,Y) in free order (paper I28). Applied at n = 0, the partial cylinders are full cylinders, and the operations Lanari built by hand come for free at a fixed cutoff q. For Lanari's specific objects one must show they are contractible; that is where the bootstrap would be reused.
speedup_targets.caveat: Borderline as reuse. If the contractibility of Lanari's cylinder objects is derived from Thm 1.1 itself, it is a corollary and does not count. It counts only if a descending induction at a cutoff supplies it for Lanari's objects without first proving Thm 1.1 at the same index. It also works only after a coskeletal cutoff; at q = infinity the descending induction has no start.

speedup_targets.title: S2. Model structure on algebraic Kan complexes (pushouts of free filler attachments are weak equivalences)
speedup_targets.statement: Algebraic Kan complexes (simplicial sets with chosen horn fillers, i.e. algebras for the free-filler monad) carry a combinatorial model structure Quillen equivalent to sSet; in particular the unit X -> free algebraic Kan complex on X, and pushouts of free horn-filler attachments, are weak equivalences.
speedup_targets.reference: Nikolaus, 'Algebraic models for higher categories', Indag. Math. 21 (2011) 52-75, arXiv:1003.1342
speedup_targets.current_size: 24 pp. (journal pages per search snippet). No Lean. Mathlib d13f23b has SSet, KanComplex, Coskeletal, AnodyneExtensions and SSet.modelCategoryQuillen classes; the OAI Thomason library (family 317) constructs a KanQuillenModel.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: This is the same obstruction in simplicial form: freely adjoining fillers creates new composites and must not change the homotopy type. The device's analogue would be a cutoff at a coskeletal level q (Mathlib has Coskeletal), with descending induction on the horn dimension, where partial Delta^1-cylinders that are stationary below n get their fillers from higher horn dimensions. Nikolaus avoids the problem by transfer, because the underlying simplicial sets are already fibrant and the free functor preserves anodyne maps. The device is therefore unnecessary and probably longer.

open_problems.title: O1. Henry's pushout conjecture / homotopy hypothesis for Grothendieck coherators OUTSIDE the Ara-Henry arity convention
open_problems.statement: Let C be a Grothendieck coherator in Maltsiniotis' general sense, where generating fillers d_j -> S may have dim(S) > j. Is every pushout of J_n along a cell of a cellular C-model a weak equivalence? Equivalently, does the homotopy hypothesis hold for all coherators, so that the theory is independent of the coherator?
open_problems.reference: Maltsiniotis 2010 (arXiv:1009.2331); Ara 2013 (arXiv:1206.2941) Secs 2.3, 2.9-2.11; Henry 2016 Sec 5.3; 312 Def 1.1 and 02-cutoffs-trees.tex:40-66
open_problems.status: open. 312 restricts to the convention; no source found resolving the general case (snippet-level).
open_problems.obstruction_match: Exact and localized. The convention is used precisely in the cutoff reflector R_q: 'If j <= q, the generating arity bound dim(S) <= j makes the tuple sets on S in X and Z identical' (02-cutoffs-trees.tex:51-53). The partial cylinders, the bootstrap and the retract argument never use it. Without the bound, an operation of output dimension j <= q may read cells above q, and R_q need not preserve cells through q, so the descending induction loses its base.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: (a) Replace R_q by a cutoff in which operations with high-arity inputs are interpreted on unique fillers. This needs the high cells to be determined, so try a two-parameter cutoff (q, q') with q' >= max arity height of the generators needed below q. That bound is finite at each tower stage, but not uniformly. (b) Alternatively, prove that every coherator receives a convention coherator by an equivalence on models that preserves J-pushouts, then transport. (c) Run the existing ExpansionContraction/cylinderPathData chain unchanged on top of the new cutoff. This is a clean device-reuse test, because only the reflector changes.
open_problems.payoff: high (removes the convention; gives coherator-independence in Maltsiniotis' generality)

open_problems.title: O2. Taylor's generalized pushout conjecture for controlled theories / infinity-Lawvere theories
open_problems.statement: For the infinity-Lawvere theories obtained as Grothendieck realizations of controlled theories (monoidal, symmetric monoidal, coherent infinity-groups, Picard infinity-groupoids), pushouts of the generating J-maps along cellular models are weak equivalences. This would give canonical semi-model structures and the corresponding homotopy hypotheses.
open_problems.reference: Taylor, 'Algebraic coherators, controlled theories, and Grothendieck realizations', arXiv:2607.28540 (Jul 2026), Conj 5.7, Thm 5.8; companion arXiv:2607.24716
open_problems.status: open (conjecture; 312 settles only the Ara-Henry Grothendieck case, which is a corollary)
open_problems.obstruction_match: It is the same pushout-of-J statement for richer globular-type theories. The device needs (i) a coskeletal cutoff that preserves low cells, which requires an arity convention for the controlled theory, (ii) groupoidal inverses for the tree/whisker contractibility, and (iii) contractible P(S) so that every generator can be interpreted in free order. Symmetric monoidal structure adds non-globular operations, so (i) and (iii) must be redone.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Check whether Taylor's algebraic coherators admit a free cellular order with an arity-height bound. If they do, the 312 chain should go through almost verbatim with the theory swapped. If not, the problem falls under O1. Monoidal or one-object cases may reduce to the Grothendieck case by suspension, which would make them corollaries.

open_problems.title: O3. Homotopy hypothesis for Batanin-Leinster weak omega-groupoids (algebras of a contractible globular operad)
open_problems.statement: For a contractible globular operad with system of compositions, the category of its groupoidal algebras, with its weak equivalences, models homotopy types.
open_problems.reference: Batanin 1998; Cisinski, 'Batanin higher groupoids and homotopy types' (2007; faithful and conservative but not full); survey status open per Henry 2016 and Henry's 2018 research statement
open_problems.obstruction_match: Batanin algebras present the same free-algebraic-structure problem, and the pushout lemma for J_n is again the crux. Ara and Bourke compare Batanin-Leinster omega-categories with Grothendieck-Maltsiniotis ones. If an analogous comparison of groupoid models lands in the Ara-Henry convention, the result is a corollary of 312. Otherwise the device must be run on operad algebras, and the obstruction is the same as in O1: operad arities are not height-bounded by output dimension.

open_problems.statement: Models of Brunerie's type theory (weak infinity-groupoids definable in dependent type theory) are equivalent, homotopically, to spaces.

Whether it meets the Ara-Henry arity bound is unverified. Coherences of output dimension j on contexts of higher dimension appear allowed, which would put it under O1. If it meets the bound, the result is a corollary of 312.

theorem_corollaries.title: Pushout lemma for (q+1)-coskeletal (cutoff) Grothendieck groupoids
theorem_corollaries.note: Internal lemma cutoff_elementary_exactBoundaryTest of the item itself. Henry-Lanari (arXiv:1905.05625; TAC 39(26) 2023, pp. 735-768) show n-groupoids and (n+1)-coskeletal infinity-groupoids have the same homotopy theory, and that a left semi-model structure on n-groupoids implies the generalized homotopy hypothesis. So the homotopy hypothesis for Grothendieck n-groupoids for every n (they did n = 3, Lanari 1809.07923 Thm 4.10 for the semi-model structure) should follow. Lean: statable with < 300 lines (truncated models); useful as an internal-consistency Lean check, not as reuse.

theorem_corollaries.title: Path object for cutoff models (Lanari's goal at finite cutoff)
theorem_corollaries.note: cylinderPathData hC q 0 gives, for each Y in A_q, a P with p_0, p_1 lifting all I_j and (p_0,p_1) lifting all J_k: a path object for fibrant objects at cutoff q. Statable now in OAI terms (∀ Y, Nonempty (CutoffPathData hC q 0 Y)). This is the device's own n = 0 instance, not reuse. Without the cutoff (q = infinity) the descending induction has no base.

family_317.title: Thomason model structures in all strict higher dimensions (25 Sep 2026; catalog row 317; comparator ThomasonModelStructures, Lean OAI/CategoryTheory/Thomason)
family_317.relation: Cites 312 as OpenAI2026 and summarizes its method (08-method-context.tex:1-28). Its own pushout argument uses positive relative prisms: strict right Gray cylinders stationary on the old sieve (03-relative-prisms.tex Lemma relative-prism; Lemma pushout-cylinder at :232-276). These glue along an arbitrary attachment via the internal hom and the pushout universal property.
family_317.is_it_device_reuse: No. It is an analogue, not a reuse of C1. (1) 317's cylinders are classical homotopies rel A: 'stationary on the old part'. They are not index-n partial cylinders and are not defined by a single joining cell at one expansion index. (2) There is no contractibility bootstrap: the strict cylinder is given by an explicit chain formula, and its gluing needs 'no injectivity, freeness, or cofibrancy hypothesis'. (3) There is no descending induction at a coskeletal cutoff; 317 notes that the strict analogue of the cutoff exists but 'supplies no comparison with Street weak equivalences'. (4) 317 states 'No result of [312] is a premise of this proof', and its appendix says the claims about 312 are not inputs. (5) Lean: no file outside OAI/CategoryTheory/Globular imports OAI.CategoryTheory.Globular, so the 317 Lean does not use 312's declarations.
family_317.what_is_shared: The high-level pattern 'control a pushout by a cylinder that is stationary on the old part and glues to the constant cylinder on the attaching target'. This is the classical homotopy-extension idea (transfer, N0), which 312 also contains.
family_317.count_for_PLAN_device_reuse_tally: 0 (record as 'analogue in the model's own manuscripts, one day later')

negative_controls.title: NC1. Two-out-of-three for weak equivalences of C-models

negative_controls.title: NC2 (proved-false analogue). The exact-boundary single-joining-cell test detects Street weak equivalences of strict omega-categories
negative_controls.statement: False: the inclusion of object 0 into 0 -> 1 <- 2 is a Street weak equivalence (terminal object), but 0 and 2 are joined by no single arrow in either direction.
negative_controls.why_device_should_not_help: The device's last step (exactBoundaryTest_of_cutoff_path, endpoint-section retract) needs groupoidal inverses and single joining cells. In directed settings the device must fail, or need a new test. 317 proves its directed pushout result without it.

negative_controls.title: NC3. Homotopy hypothesis for STRICT infinity-groupoids

The pushout lemma does hold there (Brown-Golasinski).
negative_controls.why_device_should_not_help: The device can at most deliver the pushout lemma. The homotopy hypothesis needs Henry's reduction for weak coherators. A pipeline that tries to 'prove the homotopy hypothesis with the device' for strict groupoids must fail, which separates the device from the corollary layer.

top5.target: O1 coherators outside the Ara-Henry convention
top5.score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
top5.argument: This is the best device-reuse test available. The convention is used in exactly one place, the cutoff reflector (02-cutoffs-trees.tex:51-53; exists_cutoff, dominated share about 0.06). The partial cylinders, the ExpansionContraction bootstrap and the retract argument are untouched. A Lean experiment drops the height field from AdmissiblePair, supplies a new cutoff, and measures how much of the 856-declaration DAG is reused unchanged and how much prover budget the rest takes with versus without the cylinder files in the library. Success would also settle an open question (coherator independence in Maltsiniotis' generality). Risk: no replacement cutoff exists, in which case the device does not transfer. That is informative either way.

top5.score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
top5.argument: This is a measurable speedup on a known (partial) theorem. With the device, all of Lanari's compositions, identities and inverses on cylinder cells follow from one contractibility-plus-lifting argument (I28) instead of separate constructions. It is valid at a fixed cutoff, and it counts as reuse only if the contractibility of Lanari's objects comes from the descending bootstrap rather than from Thm 1.1. Formalize Lanari's cylinder frame in the OAI GlobularFrame/CylinderNode language, then compare proof lengths and prover budget against the existing cylinderInterpretation.

top5.score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
top5.argument: This is a cross-model test of whether the device's pattern (coskeletal cutoff, descending induction on cell dimension, partial cylinders stationary below n) transfers to simplicial algebraic models. Mathlib provides SSet, horns, KanComplex, Coskeletal and the Quillen I/J classes, and family 317's OAI library supplies a KanQuillenModel. Expected speedup is low, because transfer is cheaper, so this mainly tests discoverability and generality. A null result is the expected outcome and strengthens the 'tailored device' reading.

This has the highest payoff among open problems and is the closest in form. Whether the device applies hinges on whether algebraic coherators of controlled theories admit an arity-height-bounded free order. If they do, the 312 chain should transfer almost verbatim; if not, the problem reduces to O1. It is not Lean-usable now.

A cheap syntactic check decides the case: does Brunerie's coherator meet the arity bound? If yes, the result is a corollary; if no, it is a concrete instance of O1 with a well-studied coherator, a natural first test case once O1's Lean setup exists.
